What Microsoft said
Why an administrator is needed
Your organisation decides which apps its people may use with their work or school account. Microsoft would not let you give 4Tasks access yourself, so an administrator has to allow it once.
About 4Tasks
App name: %1$s
Publisher: %1$s (%2$s)
Application (client) ID: %1$s
Redirect URI: %1$s
The one permission it asks for: %1$s
Create, read, update, and delete the signed-in user\'s tasks and task lists.

4Tasks needs it to keep the user\'s Microsoft To Do lists in step with their phone: to read them, and to save the changes made in 4Tasks. It asks for no mail, calendar or file access. It also asks for Microsoft\'s standard sign-in permissions (openid, email, offline_access and User.Read), which Microsoft lists as needing no administrator consent.
How an administrator allows it

In the Microsoft Entra admin center, open Enterprise applications, find 4Tasks and grant admin consent for the organisation. If the organisation uses the admin consent workflow, the administrator can approve the request there instead.
